open_points.subject: A04 Required test 11 and State 1 Revisions and times
open_points.text: An erasure is not one of them: it keeps no revision (rule 1).
open_points.question: State 1 says “A Customer's last-changed instant moves by: a correction of its contact, kind or fiscal data; restricting and lifting; ending and resuming the relationship; erasure.” Does Customer erasure move the last-changed instant, or does it remove the revision/last-changed pair without moving it and write only the erased-mark instant?
options: Erasure moves the last-changed instant and must have a defined corresponding revision outcome despite the record retaining no revision.
Erasure does not move the last-changed instant; it removes the revision/last-changed pair and records only the erased-mark instant.
open_points.default_guess: Erasure removes the revision and last-changed instant without moving either, and records the current instant only as the erased-mark instant.

witness.initial: A Customer has revision 7, a retained last-changed instant T0, and unerased contact data.
events: The owner erases the Customer's contact data at instant T1.
outcomes: Under State 1, erasure is an action that moves the Customer's last-changed instant, so the transition must establish a current last-changed value at T1.
Under A04 Required test 11, erasure is not an action that moves the last-changed instant and leaves no revision behind.
witness.observer: The verification check or store-transition implementation deciding what timestamp and revision effects erasure must produce.
